ground_truth.description: BaseAuth.recoverSapientSignature returns bytes32(uint256(1)) instead of actual signer imageHash, violating ISapient interface. Breaks Merkle leaf construction in BaseSig.recoverBranch.
ground_truth.root_cause: BaseAuth.recoverSapientSignature returns bytes32(uint256(1)) instead of actual signer imageHash, violating ISapient interface. Breaks Merkle leaf construction in BaseSig.recoverBranch.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: Wallet uses another wallet as sapient signer → signature validation fails due to incorrect image hash. PoC: Add test to test/modules/BaseSig.t.sol: test_BaseAuth_recoverSapientSignature_ReturnsConstant. Deploys MinimalSapient, crafts signature, asserts constant return.
ground_truth.fix_description: Return actual image hash from recoverSapientSignature. Extend signatureValidation to return imageHash or call BaseSig.recover.

vulnerabilities.type: logic_error / protocol-integration break (DoS of sapient signer flow)
vulnerabilities.explanation: recoverSapientSignature is expected (per ISapient semantics) to return the signer’s imageHash (or a value derived from the validated signature that identifies the signing configuration) so that upstream verification can construct the correct Merkle leaf/branch for sapient signers. Instead, after successfully validating the signature via signatureValidation, it returns the constant bytes32(uint256(1)). Any component that relies on this return value (e.g., Merkle leaf construction in BaseSig.recoverBranch-style logic) will compute an incorrect leaf/root and fail to validate otherwise-correct sapient signatures. This breaks wallets configured to use another wallet (sapient signer) for authorization, effectively causing a denial of service for those authorization paths and potentially locking users out of executing operations that require sapient signatures.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario:
1) A wallet configuration includes a sapient signer path (e.g., Wallet A authorizes via Wallet B using sapient signature verification).
2) When an operation is executed, the signature verification flow calls recoverSapientSignature to obtain the sapient signer’s imageHash for Merkle proof/leaf construction.
3) recoverSapientSignature returns 0x01..00 instead of the real imageHash.
4) The computed Merkle leaf/root does not match the expected signer tree, so signature verification fails.
Impact: the operation cannot be executed; if this is the required/only signing path, the wallet becomes unable to authorize actions (funds stuck / permanent DoS until configuration is changed by a valid path).
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Return the actual recovered imageHash (or the correct value required by ISapient) instead of a constant. Concretely: extend signatureValidation to also return imageHash (and possibly threshold/weight/checkpoint), or directly call BaseSig.recover(...) inside recoverSapientSignature and return the recovered imageHash after validation (and ensure the returned value matches the Merkle-leaf expectations of the sapient verification logic).

prediction.overall_explanation: The core issue is an incorrect return value in BaseAuth.recoverSapientSignature: it always returns a constant bytes32(1) even when the signature is valid. This breaks sapient signer integrations that depend on the returned imageHash to construct Merkle leaves/branches, leading to failed authorization and potential wallet operation DoS for configurations using sapient signers. No other clear, concrete unauthorized-access or fund-drain paths are evident from the provided code alone.
